gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'use your own camera' route (Wasserstein case + Blink) carries a recurring Blink Basic plan of $39.99 a year per camera (raised from $30 on 8 Oct 2025) to keep clips, against a one-off $99.99 for the Birdfy Cam 2 4K or $79.99 for the Cam 2K that clamp onto a feeder you already own.
standout_why: I compared against reviewed.com (cited, 12 feeders) and digitalcameraworld.com (top result; the fetch came back truncated). Reviewed never mentions the Birdfy Cam or Cam 2, the Wasserstein case, or using a Blink, Wyze or Ring camera at a feeder. It names Ring, Blink and Wyze only in a privacy-zone aside. It gives no frame rate for any 4K mode, and it gives subscription terms only for all-in-one feeders (Feeder 2 Pro: 7-day trial, then Birdfy Plus at $79.99/yr). The digitalcameraworld text I could read covers no camera-only add-ons and has no cost-over-time figures. WIRED (cited) would not load (fetch blocked), so I could not check it.
decides: This is partial support for the current page's pick. For a shopper who already owns a feeder, the Wasserstein case looks cheap on ChatGPT's card ($69.99), but you still need a Blink camera plus $39.99 a year per camera for the Basic plan. Over two years that is $79.98 in plan fees on top of the case and camera. The Birdfy Cam 2 4K ($99.99) or Cam 2K ($79.99) is one purchase. The page should still not say the Cam 2 needs no fees until Birdfy's own Cam 2 page confirms free bird ID and cloud. I couldn't reopen that page today.
